t: Maharaja Ranjit Singh united the feuding Sikh Misls into a single Punjab state, ruling from Lahore from 1799.
Its European-drilled army was among the strongest in India, and it governed a Muslim-majority population with a mixed-faith court.
Without institutions to manage succession, it collapsed into court intrigue after 1839 and was annexed by Britain in 1849.
dyk: Ranjit Singh had the upper storeys of the Harmandir Sahib covered in gilded copper, giving it its popular name: the Golden Temple.
ev: Ranjit Singh, aged eighteen, seizes Lahore from its Bhangi chiefs
Ranjit Singh is proclaimed Maharaja of the Punjab on Baisakhi
The Treaty of Amritsar fixes the Sutlej as the Sikh-British boundary
The Sikhs occupy Peshawar, extending the empire to the Khyber Pass
Ranjit Singh dies, leaving the Lahore court to rival factions
Defeat at Sobraon ends the First Anglo-Sikh War; Kashmir is lost
Lord Dalhousie annexes the Punjab after the Second Anglo-Sikh War
